WIDER CONTEXT
- The Rafael Viñoly building opened three years late and £9m over budget (Museums Journal, Gary Noakes, 16 February 2015). The Art Newspaper put the cost at £27m, up from an initial estimate of £17m, with £8m from the Arts Council's Lottery Fund (The Art Newspaper, Martin Bailey, 30 September 2015).
- On 12 February 2015 Arts Council England placed Firstsite under special funding arrangements and left it out of the National Portfolio for 2015-18, citing "continuing concerns" about the gallery's governance and business plans. Funding of £814,517 for one year was to be released only as milestones were met, including a viable business plan, "strong new governance" with a new chair and refreshed board, and a "viable" staffing structure (Museums Journal, 16 February 2015).
- Director Matthew Rowe declined to give the size of the deficit and said he regretted not hiring a forensic financial controller when he joined in January 2013 (Museums Journal, 16 February 2015).
- Bob Russell, the Liberal Democrat MP for the area, said he had warned at the outset that the project was not financially sustainable, and called the situation "a disgrace" and "a shambles" (Museums Journal, 16 February 2015).
- Rowe resigned in April 2015. Arts Council acting chief executive Althea Efunshile warned that Firstsite "could face the removal of our funding" unless its governance and business model improved (The Art Newspaper, 30 September 2015).

- On 28 March 2014 FACT announced a volunteer scheme for its front-of-house team, saying: "As well as retaining full-time paid staff, our Front of House team will now include volunteers," and that 11 of the 13 staff of the previous team were continuing in paid roles (FACT, 28 March 2014).
- The Double Negative reported that the previous front-of-house team had nine casual staff on zero-hour contracts, three part-time staff, one full-time member and 21 volunteers, and the new structure three full-time staff, six casual staff, no part-time roles and 71 volunteers. - Five affected staff, speaking anonymously, said their main complaint was how the changes were handled and communicated. One said: "The front of house team were not involved in any reviews or restructures to offer input, suggestions or alternatives" (The Double Negative, 7 May 2014).
- Executive Director Iona Horsburgh said the decision responded to supply and demand, that a full consultation took place, and: "We knew that we needed to restructure the department" (The Double Negative, 7 May 2014).
- Liverpool IWW and Liverpool Class Action announced a picket of FACT for 1 May 2014, calling for "the reinstatement of the sacked FACT staff" alongside support for striking Ritzy cinema workers in London (Liverpool IWW, 28 April 2014).
- Unverified: FACT had decided to make eleven front-of-house staff redundant and replace them with unpaid volunteers, from Liverpool IWW, a trade union branch.
